title: One time in Deira: starting a story
goal: At a karak stand, tell Sēf a funny story from your first week in Dubai, starting it with marra min il-marrāt
tip: Open a story with marra min il-marrāt 'once, one time'. Move it on with lamma + a past verb 'when': lamma ṭalabt 'when I ordered'. Give the turn with gām + a verb: gām ykallimni bil-ingilīzi 'he started talking to me in English'.
grammar: recycle: lamma + past, gām + verb, kān gāʿid; opening a story (marra min il-marrāt)
dialogue: A
خبرني، كيف كان أول أسبوع لك في دبي؟
khabbirni, chēf kān awwal usbūʿ lak fi Dbayy?
Tell me, how was your first week in Dubai?
B
والله كان غريب! مرة من المرات، رحت مطعم في ديرة
wallāh kān gharīb! marra min il-marrāt, riḥt maṭʿam fi Dēra
Honestly, it was strange! One time, I went to a restaurant in Deira.
A
زين، وشو السالفة؟
zēn, w shu s-sālfa?
OK, and what's the story?
B
لما طلبت، قلت بالعربي: أبي عصير لو سمحت
lamma ṭalabt, gilt bil-ʿarabi: abi ʿaṣīr law samaḥt
When I ordered, I said in Arabic: 'I'd like a juice, please.'
A
ما شاء الله عليك! وفهم؟
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! w fihim?
Good for you! And did he understand?
B
هيه، بس قام يكلمني بالإنقليزي!
hē, bas gām ykallimni bil-ingilīzi!
Yes, but he started talking to me in English!
A
كلهم جي! وانت شو قلت له؟
killhum chī! w inta shu gilt-lah?
They're all like that! And what did you say to him?
B
قلت له: أنا قاعد أتعلم عربي! وقام يضحك علي
gilt-lah: ana gāʿid atʿallam ʿarabi! w gām yiẓḥak ʿalay
I told him: 'I'm learning Arabic!' And he started laughing at me.
items: once, one time (to start a story)
the first day: awwal yōm (أول يوم)
when I ordered; when you ordered (to a man)
to a woman: lamma ṭalabti (لما طلبتي)
I said (it) in Arabic; you said (it) in Arabic (to a man)
to a woman: gilti bil-ʿarabi (قلتي بالعربي)
she started talking to me: gāmat tkallimni (قامت تكلمني)
what did you say to him? (to a man)
to a woman: shu giltī-lah? (شو قلتي له؟)
I'm learning Arabic (said by a man)
a woman says: gāʿda atʿallam ʿarabi (قاعدة أتعلم عربي)
culture: A story or a chat is a sālfa (سالفة), and to chat or tell one is ysōlif. Friends keep a story going with w baʿdēn? 'and then?' and wallāh? 'really?', so expect to be interrupted: it means they're listening.

title: Suddenly the power went off
goal: At the office, tell Maryam why you look so tired: you got stuck in your building's lift last night
tip: fajʼa 'suddenly' marks the turn in a story, and the verb after it is past: w fajʼa ingiṭʿat il-kahraba 'and suddenly the power went off'. Set the scene first with kān + a participle: kint rājiʿ il-bēt 'I was on my way home'.
grammar: recycle: kān + participle (kint rājiʿ), gām + verb; the turn in a story (fajʼa)
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. شفيك؟ شكلك تعبان
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. shfīk? shaklak taʿbān
Good morning. What's wrong? You look tired.
B
صباح النور. البارحة صار لي شي غريب
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. il-bārḥa ṣār-li shay gharīb
Good morning. Something strange happened to me last night.
A
خير إن شاء الله؟ شي خطير؟
khēr in shāʼ allāh? shay khaṭīr?
Nothing bad, I hope? Something serious?
B
كنت راجع البيت من الشغل، ودخلت اللفت
kint rājiʿ il-bēt min ish-shughul, w dakhalt il-lift
I was on my way home from work, and I got into the lift.
A
وبعدين؟ لا تقول إنه وقف!
w baʿdēn? la tgūl innah wigaf!
And then? Don't tell me it stopped!
B
هيه! فجأة انقطعت الكهربا، واللفت وقف بين الطوابق
hē! fajʼa ingiṭʿat il-kahraba, w il-lift wigaf bēn iṭ-ṭawābig
Yes! Suddenly the power went off, and the lift stopped between floors.
A
يا ساتر! وكم قعدت داخل؟
yā sātir! w cham gaʿadt dākhil?
Good grief! And how long were you in there?
B
نص ساعة، تصدقين؟ قمت أصارخ وأدق الباب!
nuṣṣ sāʿa, tṣaddgīn? gimt aṣārikh w adigg il-bāb!
Half an hour, can you believe it? I started shouting and banging on the door!
items: to us: ṣār-lna shay gharīb (صار لنا شي غريب)
I was on my way home (said by a man)
a woman says: kint rājʿa l-bēt (كنت راجعة البيت)
I got into the lift; you got into the lift (to a man)
to a woman: dakhalti l-lift (دخلتي اللفت)
he shouts: yṣārikh (يصارخ); gimt aṣārikh = I started shouting
good grief! oh my God! (a shock or a scare)
I knock on the door, I bang on the door
can you believe it? would you believe it? (to a woman)

title: In the end it was in my pocket
goal: At a café, tell Fahad and Sēf how you lost your car key at the beach, and how the story ended
tip: bil-akhīr 'in the end, finally' brings a story to its end, like ākhir shay. ṭilaʿ 'he went out' also means 'it turned out (to be)': ṭilaʿ fi jēbi 'it turned out to be in my pocket'. To a group: tadrūn …? 'do you know …?'
grammar: recycle: lamma + past, gām + verb; ending a story (bil-akhīr; ṭilaʿ 'it turned out')
dialogue: B
تدرون شو صار لي يوم الجمعة في البحر؟
tadrūn shu ṣār-li yōm il-jumʿa fi l-baḥar?
Do you know what happened to me at the beach on Friday?
A
لا والله. شنو صار؟
la wallāh. shinu ṣār?
No idea. What happened?
B
لما طلعت من الماي، ما لقيت مفتاح السيارة!
lamma ṭilaʿt min il-māy, ma ligēt miftāḥ is-sayyāra!
When I came out of the water, I couldn't find the car key!
A
أفا! يمكن طاح منك في الماي!
afa! yimkin ṭāḥ minnak fi l-māy!
Oh no! Maybe it fell out in the water!
B
دورت ساعة كاملة، والناس قاموا يدورون وياي
dawwart sāʿa kāmla, w in-nās gāmaw ydawwrūn wiyyāy
I looked for a whole hour, and people started looking with me.
A
زين، وبالأخير لقيته؟
zēn, w bil-akhīr ligētah?
OK, and in the end did you find it?
B
هيه! طلع في جيبي من الأول! تصدقون؟
hē! ṭilaʿ fi jēbi min il-awwal! tṣaddgūn?
Yes! It turned out it had been in my pocket all along! Can you believe it?
A
صج؟! والله ضحكتني حيل!
ṣij?! wallāh ẓaḥḥaktni ḥēl!
Really?! Honestly, you've made me laugh so much!
items: also: fi l-akhīr (في الأخير); like ākhir shay 'in the end'
do you know what happened to me? (to a group)
to one man: tadri shu ṣār-li? (تدري شو صار لي؟); to one woman: tadrīn shu ṣār-li?
I couldn't find, I didn't find; you didn't find (to a man)
to a woman: ma ligēti (ما لقيتي)
it turned out to be in my pocket
ṭilaʿ = it (m.) turned out; ṭilʿat = it (f.) turned out
he started looking: gām ydawwir (قام يدور)
you made me laugh (to a man)
to a woman: ẓaḥḥaktīni (ضحكتيني); to a group: ẓaḥḥaktūni (ضحكتوني)
culture: Fahad says ḥēl 'so much, very', where Sēf would say wāyid: ḥēl is the more Kuwaiti word, and you'll hear it from Fahad and Nūra. afa! 'oh no!' is said all over the Gulf when you hear bad news.

title: Are you kidding? Reacting to a story
goal: At university, Sēf tells you how he helped an old man whose car had broken down; keep him going and react to the twist
tip: A good listener keeps the story going: w baʿdēn? kammil! 'and then? go on!', and reacts to the twist: titghashmar? 'are you kidding?', mub maʿgūl! 'no way!'. Participles set the scene: shift shēba wāgif 'I saw an old man standing'.
grammar: recycle: participles in a story (rājiʿ, wāgif); listener phrases (kammil!, titghashmar?)
dialogue: A
اسمع هالسالفة! أمس كنت راجع من البر
ismaʿ has-sālfa! ams kint rājiʿ min il-barr
Listen to this! Yesterday I was coming back from the desert.
B
هيه، وبعدين؟ كمل!
hē, w baʿdēn? kammil!
Yes, and then? Go on!
A
شفت شيبة واقف يم سيارته، وسيارته خربانة
shift shēba wāgif yamm sayyārtah, w sayyārtah kharbāna
I saw an old man standing by his car, and his car had broken down.
B
مسكين! وانت وقّفت له؟
maskīn! w inta waggaft-lah?
Poor man! And did you stop for him?
A
هيه، ووصّلته بيته. وبالأخير، تدري منو طلع؟
hē, w waṣṣaltah bētah. w bil-akhīr, tadri minu ṭilaʿ?
Yes, and I gave him a lift home. And in the end, do you know who he turned out to be?
B
منو؟ قول!
minu? gūl!
Who? Tell me!
A
الدكتور اليديد حقنا! تصدق؟ وشافني اليوم في المحاضرة
id-daktōr il-yidīd ḥaggna! tṣaddig? w shāfni l-yōm fi l-muḥāẓra
Our new lecturer! Can you believe it? And he saw me today in the lecture.
B
تتغشمر؟! مب معقول!
titghashmar?! mub maʿgūl!
Are you kidding?! No way!
items: to a woman: ismaʿi has-sālfa (اسمعي هالسالفة)
go on! carry on! (to a man)
also: shāyib (شايب); speak to him as yā ʿammi
I stopped for him (in the car); you stopped for him (to a man)
I gave him a lift, I dropped him off; you gave him a lift (to a man)
do you know who he turned out to be? (to a man)
to a woman: tadrīn minu ṭilaʿ? (تدرين منو طلع؟)
are you kidding? are you joking? (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: titghashmarīn? (تتغشمرين؟); with an elder, say ṣij? or wallāh?
no way! I can't believe it!

title: Juḥa's donkey: telling a joke
goal: At a desert camp, tell Sēf and the guys a Juḥa joke and get the punchline right
tip: A joke is told like a story, in the past, with marra min il-marrāt and fajʼa. The punchline is often a quote: Juḥa gāl: tṣaddig il-ḥmār w ma tṣaddigni? 'you believe the donkey and not me?'. To a group: tabūn agūl-lkum nukta? 'shall I tell you a joke?'
grammar: recycle: storytelling (marra min il-marrāt, fajʼa); quoting speech in a joke
dialogue: B
يا شباب، تبون أقول لكم نكتة؟
yā shabāb, tabūn agūl-lkum nukta?
Guys, shall I tell you a joke?
A
يلا، قول! بس لا تكون بايخة!
yalla, gūl! bas la tkūn bāykha!
Go on, tell it! Just don't let it be a lame one!
B
مرة من المرات، جار جحا قال له: عطني الحمار شوي
marra min il-marrāt, jār Juḥa gāl-lah: ʿaṭni l-ḥmār shwayy
Once, Juḥa's neighbour said to him: 'Lend me the donkey for a bit.'
A
وجحا شو قال له؟
w Juḥa shu gāl-lah?
And what did Juḥa say to him?
B
قال: آسف، الحمار مب هني. وفجأة سمعوا صوت الحمار!
gāl: āsif, il-ḥmār mub hni. w fajʼa simʿaw ṣōt il-ḥmār!
He said: 'Sorry, the donkey's not here.' And suddenly they heard the sound of the donkey!
A
والجار شو قال؟
w il-jār shu gāl?
And what did the neighbour say?
B
قال: أسمع الحمار! وجحا قال: تصدق الحمار وما تصدقني؟
gāl: asmaʿ il-ḥmār! w Juḥa gāl: tṣaddig il-ḥmār w ma tṣaddigni?
He said: 'I can hear the donkey!' And Juḥa said: 'You believe the donkey and not me?'
A
والله ضحكتنا! نكتة حلوة
wallāh ẓaḥḥaktna! nukta ḥilwa
You've really made us laugh! That's a good one.
items: shall I tell you? do you want me to tell you? (to a group)
to one man: tabi agūl-lak? (تبي أقول لك؟); to one woman: tabīn agūl-lich?
my neighbour: jāri (جاري); UAE also: il-yār (اليار); you've met jārna (جارنا) 'our neighbour'
his donkey: ḥmārah (حماره); never call a person this: it's an insult
what did he say to him?
to her: shu gāl-lha? (شو قال لها؟)
you don't believe me (to a man)
to a woman: ma tṣaddgīni (ما تصدقيني)
you made us laugh (to a man)
culture: Juḥa (جحا) is the wise fool of Arab folk tales, and many of his stories are also told about Nasreddin in Turkey and Iran. This one, 'you believe the donkey and not me?', is told about both of them.

title: I nearly missed my flight
goal: Back from London, tell Bū Rāshid in his majlis, with Sēf there, how you nearly missed your flight, from start to finish
tip: A longer story strings it all together: the scene with kān, lamma for 'when', fajʼa for the turn, gām for what you started doing, bil-akhīr for the end. kān b- says what nearly happened: iṭ-ṭayyāra kānat bitfūtni 'I nearly missed my flight'.
grammar: recycle: kān b- 'nearly', lamma, fajʼa, gām + verb, bil-akhīr in one story
dialogue: A
الحمد لله على السلامة يا ولدي. كيف كانت لندن؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma yā wildi. chēf kānat Landan?
Welcome back, son. How was London?
B
الله يسلمك يا عمي. حلوة، بس الطيارة كانت بتفوتني!
allāh ysallmak yā ʿammi. ḥilwa, bas iṭ-ṭayyāra kānat bitfūtni!
Thank you, uncle. Lovely, but I nearly missed my flight!
A
يا ساتر! ليش يا ولدي؟ شو صار؟
yā sātir! lēsh yā wildi? shu ṣār?
Good grief! Why, son? What happened?
B
تخيل يا عمي! لما قمت من النوم كانت الساعة ست
tkhayyal yā ʿammi! lamma gimt min in-nōm kānat is-sāʿa sitt
Just imagine, uncle! When I woke up, it was six o'clock.
A
ست؟! والطيارة الساعة كم؟
sitt?! w iṭ-ṭayyāra s-sāʿa cham?
Six?! And what time was the flight?
B
ثمان! خذت تاكسي، وفجأة الشارع كله زحمة!
thamān! khadht tāksi, w fajʼa sh-shāriʿ killah zaḥma!
Eight! I got a taxi, and suddenly the whole road was jammed!
A
أفا! ووصلت على الوقت؟
afa! w wiṣalt ʿala l-wagt?
Oh no! And did you get there on time?
B
قمت أركض في المطار، وبالأخير الطيارة طلعت متأخرة!
gimt arkiẓ fi l-maṭār, w bil-akhīr iṭ-ṭayyāra ṭilʿat mitʼakhkhra!
I started running through the airport, and in the end the flight turned out to be late!
items: I nearly missed my flight (lit. the plane was about to miss me)
I woke up, I got up; you got up (to a man)
to a woman: gimti min in-nōm (قمتي من النوم)
I got a taxi; you got a taxi (to a man)
to a woman: khadhti tāksi (خذتي تاكسي)
he started running: gām yirkiẓ (قام يركض)

title: Checkpoint 3.7: a surprise lunch for Khālid
goal: Checkpoint (stage review): at the office, tell Maryam that a colleague is leaving, and plan a surprise lunch with her
tip: Stage 3 review, and now you say it: news with gāl-li innah + a participle (ṭāliʿ), ma adri wēn biyrūḥ, lō ana makānah, chān gaʿadt 'if I were him, I'd stay', illi + -ah (illi yḥibbah), maḥjūz 'booked up', ittaṣalt, and to a woman khallīni attaṣil 'let me ring'.
grammar: checkpoint 3.7 (stage review): participle, reported speech, ma adri, lō … chān, illi, maḥjūz, ittaṣalt, khalli + verb
dialogue: B
سمعتي؟ خالد قال لي إنه طالع من الشركة
simaʿti? Khālid gāl-li innah ṭāliʿ min ish-sharika
Have you heard? Khālid told me he's leaving the company.
A
مب معقول! ليش؟ لقى شغل ثاني؟
mub maʿgūl! lēsh? liga shughul thāni?
No way! Why? Has he found another job?
B
هيه، بس ما أدري وين بيروح. لو أنا مكانه، جان قعدت!
hē, bas ma adri wēn biyrūḥ. lō ana makānah, chān gaʿadt!
Yes, but I don't know where he's going. If I were him, I'd stay!
A
خسارة! خلنا نسوي له غدا قبل لا يطلع
khasāra! khallna nsawwī-lah ghada gabil la yiṭlaʿ
What a shame! Let's put on a lunch for him before he leaves.
B
فكرة حلوة! بس المطعم اللي يحبه دوم محجوز
fikra ḥilwa! bas il-maṭʿam illi yḥibbah dōm maḥjūz
Good idea! But the restaurant he likes is always booked up.
A
عادي، اتصل فيهم الحين. يمكن تلقى طاولة
ʿādi, ittaṣil fīhum il-ḥīn. yimkin tilga ṭāwla
Never mind, ring them now. Maybe you'll get a table.
B
اتصلت فيهم من قبل، وبالأخير ما لقيت. خليني أتصل مرة ثانية
ittaṣalt fīhum min gabil, w bil-akhīr ma ligēt. khallīni attaṣil marra thānya
I've rung them before, and in the end I never got one. Let me ring again.
A
زين. بس لا تقول له، خلها مفاجأة!
zēn. bas la tgūl-lah, khallha mufājaʼa!
OK. But don't tell him, keep it a surprise!
items: after lō: lō ana makānah, chān gaʿadt = if I were him, I'd stay
he found a job, he's got a job
I found a job: ligēt shughul (لقيت شغل); she found a job: ligat shughul (لقت شغل)
maybe you'll get a table (to a man)
to a woman: yimkin tilgīn ṭāwla (يمكن تلقين طاولة)
let me ring, let me call (to a woman)
to a man: khallni attaṣil (خلني أتصل)
before she leaves: gabil la tiṭlaʿ (قبل لا تطلع)
keep it a surprise (to a man)
to a woman: khallīha mufājaʼa (خليها مفاجأة)

title: B1 exit: chatting with a stranger
goal: B1 exit: at a café, an Emirati at the next table hears you order in Arabic and starts chatting; talk about yourself, Dubai and football
tip: Unprepared talk runs on short answers with a reason, then a question back: b-raʼyi n-nās, lann kill illi shift-hum ṭayybīn… w inta? Add a plan: idha ligēt shughul, bagʿid hni. When someone agrees with you, you'll hear ṣidagt wallāh! 'too true!'.
grammar: B1 exit: unprepared conversation on a familiar topic (opinion + reason, idha, illi, ma ʿād)
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم. ما شاء الله، تتكلم عربي!
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. mā shāʼ allāh, titkallam ʿarabi!
Peace be upon you. Wow, you speak Arabic!
B
وعليكم السلام. شوي شوي، للحين أتعلم
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. shwayy shwayy, lil-ḥīn atʿallam
And upon you peace. Bit by bit; I'm still learning.
A
من وين انت؟ وشو يابك دبي؟
min wēn inta? w shu yābak Dbayy?
Where are you from? And what brought you to Dubai?
B
من لندن. ييت أدرس وأتدرب، وإذا لقيت شغل بقعد هني
min Landan. yīt adris w atdarrab, w idha ligēt shughul bagʿid hni
From London. I came to study and do an internship, and if I find a job, I'll stay here.
A
حلو! شو رأيك، شو أحسن شي في دبي؟
ḥilu! shu raʼyak, shu aḥsan shay fi Dbayy?
Nice! What do you think, what's the best thing about Dubai?
B
برأيي الناس، لأن كل اللي شفتهم طيبين
b-raʼyi n-nās, lann kill illi shift-hum ṭayybīn
In my opinion, the people, because everyone I've met is nice.
A
صدقت والله! وتحب الكورة؟ تشجّع أي فريق؟
ṣidagt wallāh! w tḥibb il-kūra? tshajjiʿ ay farīg?
Too true! And do you like football? Which team do you support?
B
أشجّع فريق من لندن، بس ما عاد أشوف الكورة وايد. وانت؟
ashajjiʿ farīg min Landan, bas ma ʿād ashūf il-kūra wāyid. w inta?
I support a London team, but I don't watch football much any more. And you?
items: to a woman: shu yābich? (شو يابج؟); you'll see written جابك
everyone I've met, all the people I've seen
everything I've seen: kill illi shiftah (كل اللي شفته)
too true! you're so right! (to a man)
to a woman: ṣidagti wallāh! (صدقتي والله)
do you like football? (to a man)
to a woman: tḥibbīn il-kūra? (تحبين الكورة؟)
you support: tshajjiʿ (تشجّع) to a man, tshajjʿīn (تشجّعين) to a woman; a team: farīg (فريق)

title: B1 exit: my first day at work
goal: B1 exit: two years into your internship, tell Maryam and the team the story of your first day at the office
tip: Tell it in order: the scene with kān (ma kint aʿarf aḥad, wala kint adri shu l-mafrūẓ asawwi; kint gāʿid asmaʿ 'I was sitting there listening'), the turn with fajʼa, what started with gām (gimt arjif), and the end with bil-akhīr. To a woman, 'do you remember?' is tidhkrīn?
grammar: B1 exit: narrate an experience (lamma, kān gāʿid + verb, fajʼa, gām + verb, bil-akhīr)
dialogue: A
تدري إن اليوم صار لك سنتين ويانا؟
tadri inn il-yōm ṣār-lak santēn wiyyāna?
Did you know you've been with us two years today?
B
سنتين؟! والله ما حسيت. تذكرين أول يوم لي؟
santēn?! wallāh ma ḥassēt. tidhkrīn awwal yōm li?
Two years?! Honestly, it doesn't feel like it. Do you remember my first day?
A
أكيد! بس قول لهم انت، شو صار؟
akīd! bas gūl-lhum inta, shu ṣār?
Of course! But you tell them what happened.
B
لما ييت، ما كنت أعرف أحد، ولا كنت أدري شو المفروض أسوي
lamma yīt, ma kint aʿarf aḥad, wala kint adri shu l-mafrūẓ asawwi
When I came, I didn't know anyone, and I didn't know what I was supposed to do.
A
وفي الاجتماع؟
w fi l-ijtimāʿ?
And in the meeting?
B
كنت قاعد أسمع بس، وفجأة المدير قال لي: تكلم عن نفسك بالعربي!
kint gāʿid asmaʿ bas, w fajʼa l-mudīr gāl-li: tkallam ʿan nafsak bil-ʿarabi!
I was just sitting there listening, and suddenly the manager said to me: 'Talk about yourself in Arabic!'
A
صح! وشو قلت؟
ṣaḥḥ! w shu gilt?
That's right! And what did you say?
B
قمت أرجف! بس بالأخير قلت: اسمي سالم! والكل قام يصفق
gimt arjif! bas bil-akhīr gilt: ismi Sālim! w il-kill gām yṣaffig
I started shaking! But in the end I said: 'My name's Sālim!' And everyone started clapping.
